children.text: In 1765, British clockmaker James Cox invented a clock whose only source of energy is the fluctuations in atmospheric pressure. Use uniform gravity \(g=9.8\,\mathrm{m/s^2}\), incompressible liquids, no surface tension, constant ambient temperature and isothermal transformations. Atmospheric pressure is uniform with height. Part A uses a thin-walled vertical cylinder, open at the bottom and closed at the top, length H=1 m, area \(S=10\,\mathrm{cm^2}\), mass m=0.5 kg, in a semi-infinite bath whose surface is z=0. The top has altitude h and internal liquid surface altitude zl. Initially h=zl=0 and no gas is trapped. Lift it slowly until its bottom reaches the bath level. Outside pressure is \(P_0=10^5\,\mathrm{Pa}\).

children.text: Use the original pulley diagram. A finite cistern and two-part tube hang from cables attached to opposite sides of a mass M sliding horizontally with friction magnitude Fs and stops at x=plus or minus X. Initially x=0 and P1=0 balance. The cistern has area Sc=210 square centimetres, height 30 cm, and the total mercury volume is 5 L. Keep the tube dimensions above. Assume its bottom stays submerged and its liquid level stays inside the bulb. Let \(\xi=(S_b+S_c-S_t)F_s/(S_bS_cA)\), with St negligible compared with Sb,Sc. Find the threshold above which the mass always remains at rest.
Temporarily block M at x=X and set P1=0. Find the resultant cable tension along x.

For xi below threshold define \(\lambda=2(S_b-S_t)\rho gX/(S_bA)\simeq2\rho gX/A\). Classify the two regimes and sketch x(t)/X over three weeks against the triangular pressure wave. Neglect switching time compared with one week.
In the switching steady regime, W is the frictional work per pressure period. With Sb approximately Sc and negligible St, optimize Fs and X and find Wstar numerically.
Find the atmospheric pressure work in the optimal cycle and the ratio of recovered work to it. A P-V plot may help.

statement.text:
Cox's Timepiece
In 1765, British clockmaker James Cox invented a clock whose only source of energy is the fluctuations in atmospheric pressure. Use uniform gravity \(g=9.8\,\mathrm{m/s^2}\), incompressible liquids, no surface tension, constant ambient temperature and isothermal transformations. Atmospheric pressure is uniform with height. Part A uses a thin-walled vertical cylinder, open at the bottom and closed at the top, length H=1 m, area \(S=10\,\mathrm{cm^2}\), mass m=0.5 kg, in a semi-infinite bath whose surface is z=0. The top has altitude h and internal liquid surface altitude zl. Initially h=zl=0 and no gas is trapped. Lift it slowly until its bottom reaches the bath level. Outside pressure is \(P_0=10^5\,\mathrm{Pa}\).
A.1. Submerged-tube force

Before vapour appears, find water pressure at the top and upward force F holding the tube.
A.2. Three water temperatures

For water at 20,80,99 degrees Celsius use respectively densities 1000,970,960 kg/m cubed and saturated vapour pressures 2340,47400,99800 Pa. Determine whether F rises throughout lifting, or levels off at a height hstar. Find maximal force and any accessible hstar.
A.3. Mercury vapour correction
Replace water by mercury at 20 degrees Celsius, density 13500 kg/m cubed and Psat=0.163 Pa. Find relative error in maximal force if Psat is ignored.
B.1. Added mercury mass

Now neglect mercury vapour. A two-part tube has lower area St and height Ht=80 cm, and top bulb area Sb greater than St and height Hb=20 cm. Let ht be junction altitude. Its holding force is \((m_{tb}+m_{add})g\). Identify the mercury volume responsible for madd.
B.2. Added mass versus lift
At fixed P0 lift from fully immersed to ht=Ht. Sketch madd versus ht, including slopes and breakpoints.
B.3. Pressure-driven mass amplitude

Fix ht so the liquid is midway up the bulb at mean P0. Pressure perturbation P1 is a triangular wave of amplitude A=500 Pa and period one week. Use St=5 square centimetres and Sb=200 square centimetres. Find mass-variation amplitude while the surface stays inside the bulb.
C.1. Motion threshold

Use the original pulley diagram. A finite cistern and two-part tube hang from cables attached to opposite sides of a mass M sliding horizontally with friction magnitude Fs and stops at x=plus or minus X. Initially x=0 and P1=0 balance. The cistern has area Sc=210 square centimetres, height 30 cm, and the total mercury volume is 5 L. Keep the tube dimensions above. Assume its bottom stays submerged and its liquid level stays inside the bulb. Let \(\xi=(S_b+S_c-S_t)F_s/(S_bS_cA)\), with St negligible compared with Sb,Sc. Find the threshold above which the mass always remains at rest.
C.2. Tension at the stop
Temporarily block M at x=X and set P1=0. Find the resultant cable tension along x.
C.3. Operating regimes
For xi below threshold define \(\lambda=2(S_b-S_t)\rho gX/(S_bA)\simeq2\rho gX/A\). Classify the two regimes and sketch x(t)/X over three weeks against the triangular pressure wave. Neglect switching time compared with one week.
C.4. Optimal recovered energy
In the switching steady regime, W is the frictional work per pressure period. With Sb approximately Sc and negligible St, optimize Fs and X and find Wstar numerically.
C.5. Atmospheric work and efficiency
Find the atmospheric pressure work in the optimal cycle and the ratio of recovered work to it. A P-V plot may help.

children.text: Hydrostatic balance gives \(P_w=P_0-\rho gh\). The top cap experiences downward pressure difference \((P_0-P_w)S\). Thus \(F=mg+\rho gSh\), upward along z.

Vapour appears when \(P_w=P_{sat}\), so \(h_*= (P_0-P_{sat})/(\rho g)\). If this exceeds H, force rises to \((m+\rho SH)g\). At 20 C, hstar=9.97 m, inaccessible, Fmax=14.7 N. At 80 C, hstar=5.53 m, inaccessible, Fmax=14.4 N. At 99 C, hstar=0.0213 m, accessible, and Fmax=mg+S(P0-Psat)=5.10 N. The first two follow behaviour A, the third behaviour B.
The true maximum is \(mg+S(P_0-P_{sat})\). Neglecting vapour increases it by \(SP_{sat}\), giving \[\epsilon=\frac{SP_{sat}}{mg+S(P_0-P_{sat})}\simeq1.55\times10^{-6}.\]

It is the mercury inside the tube above the outside bath surface. Shade that region up to the internal liquid level. The empty tube weight is already included in mtb. Mercury below the bath surface does not contribute added load in the thin-wall model.

Let \(z_*=P_0/(\rho g)=0.756\,\mathrm m\). The four segments are \[m_{add}=\begin{cases}\rho S_b(h_t+H_b),&-H_b\le h_t\le0,\\\rho(S_bH_b+S_th_t),&0\le h_t\le z_*-H_b,\\\rho[S_th_t+S_b(z_*-h_t)],&z_*-H_b\le h_t\le z_*,\\\rho S_tz_*,&z_*\le h_t\le H_t.\end{cases}\] Slopes are \(\rho S_b,\rho S_t,-\rho(S_b-S_t),0\). They join continuously at 0, zstar-Hb, zstar.
The internal level changes by \(P_1/(\rho g)\), so added mass changes by \(S_bP_1/g\). Its amplitude is \(S_bA/g=1.020\,\mathrm{kg}\).

At fixed x, pressure P1 transfers apparent load between containers. Hydrostatic balance and volume conservation give the net tension \[T_P=\frac{2S_bS_c}{S_b+S_c-S_t}P_1.\] Its maximum magnitude is this coefficient times A. Static friction can hold throughout if xi is greater than 2. Thus \(\xi_*=2\). Equality is the marginal threshold.

The container displacements are opposite because of the cables. Solve equal liquid-level shift and mercury-volume conservation to find the cistern apparent-mass change \(-2\rho S_c(S_b-S_t)X/(S_b+S_c-S_t)\). Its opposite is the tube load change, hence \[T=\frac{4S_c(S_b-S_t)}{S_b+S_c-S_t}\rho gX\simeq\frac{4S_bS_c}{S_b+S_c}\rho gX.\] It is positive, towards the same stop, not a restoring force.

General tension is \(T=C_P[P_1+2\rho g(S_b-S_t)x/S_b]\), with \(C_P=2S_bS_c/(S_b+S_c-S_t)\). Initially motion starts when P1/A exceeds xi/2 and rapidly reaches +X. If \(\xi+2\lambda>2\), even the most negative pressure cannot release it from that stop, so it stays there. If \(\xi+2\lambda<2\), it repeatedly switches between the stops. Draw an initial 0 plateau, then +1. In the switching regime it settles to a rectangular wave between +1 and -1 with the forcing period and equal dwell times. The equality is a marginal switching limit. No inertial trajectory is specified by this slow-switching approximation.

The total distance per cycle is 4X, so \(W=4F_sX\). The switching boundary is \(F_s/(S_cA)+2\rho gX/A\le1\). The optimum is approached at \[X_*=A/(4\rho g),\quad F_{s,*}=AS_c/2,\quad W_*=A^2S_c/(2\rho g).\] With the stated values, Xstar=0.945 mm, Fsstar=5.25 N, and Wstar=19.84 mJ. In an exactly quasistatic model the boundary is marginal, so this is the limiting maximum approached from the switching side.

In the equal-area approximation the exposed system volume change is \(V_1=-S_c[x+P_1/(2\rho g)]\). Over the cycle \(W_{pr}=-\oint P_1dV_1\). At optimum switches occur at pressure extrema. The P1-V1 parallelogram has height 2A and horizontal width \(2S_cX_*\), giving \[W_{pr,*}=4AS_cX_*=S_cA^2/(\rho g)=39.68\,\mathrm{mJ},\quad W_*/W_{pr,*}=1/2.\]
